threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still refer to the overground as a 'train,' and you haven't yet figured out the real difference between a 'coffee shop' and a 'cafe.'
Last night on the N199, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 80s hits. No one complained, just everyone chimed in on the choruses.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing kickball in the street while their parents argued in a mix of Turkish and German – that’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a bus full of artists heading to a spontaneous gallery opening at 2 AM—only in Berlin does public transport double as a cultural lifeline.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they nonchalantly step over the giant puddles in the streets, while newcomers scan for the least splashy route.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus where the driver stopped to let a guy finish his rap before rolling out. Gotta love the little respects in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think wines in Gràcia are overpriced, but the best bottles are often sold in tiny shops tucked between bakeries and art galleries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their confused look when they see the ‘Tapa de Sants’ sign. It's a classic locals-only code for the metro!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for directions to the nearest tube and everyone points you to a bus stop instead. Clearly, you haven't figured out 'it's quicker on the 30.'
Caught the N155 last night and some bloke was trying to sell a selfie stick. Said it was 'for capturing the night.' Just another typical journey.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a group of guys outside my window debating the pros and cons of falafel spots at 3am, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find graffiti-covered buses doubling as art spaces, a testament to the city's wild blend of chaos and creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local would know to avoid 16th and Mission during rush hour unless you want to witness a spontaneous street performance of chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy at the Muni stop serenading pigeons with an old guitar. They seemed into it—one even fluffed its feathers like it was grooving.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can get an acai bowl anywhere, but locals know that the best smoothies are at the hidden fruit stall on Carrer de Fraternitat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their puzzled looks at the ticket machines. Locals zip through without a second glance, while newcomers are still deciphering the options.
